subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core bootstrap context selector for this cluster, and should dynamic command-generated bootstrap content be core-owned or left to plugin/hook surfaces?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the answer creates public config/API semantics and may introduce pre-prompt command execution, so automation should not choose the product or security boundary.

options.title: Narrow Core Selector
options.body: Accept an additive session-type bootstrap selector in core while keeping command-generated dynamic context in plugin/hook surfaces with explicit security controls.

options.title: Unified Bootstrap Engine
options.body: Design a broader core bootstrap engine that covers selectors, arbitrary files, dynamic command expansion, and live-time behavior together before landing partial PRs.

options.title: Decline New Core Surface
options.body: Keep fixed filters and cache-stable prompt time, and steer dynamic or computed context to existing plugin hooks and ClawHub packages.

recommendation.title: Narrow Core Selector
recommendation.body: Accept an additive session-type bootstrap selector in core while keeping command-generated dynamic context in plugin/hook surfaces with explicit security controls.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history on subagent bootstrap limiting and prior maintainer-side review of the related tiered-bootstrap direction.
